title: Eight Billion People
objective: After this level you can explain how the world population grew and where people live today.
summary: About 1 billion people lived on Earth around 1800; 8 billion by 2022, thanks to longer lives. Growth is slowing, and people cluster in Asia and north of the Equator.

cards.headline: Around 1800, the world held about 1 billion people. Now it holds 8.
cards.body: It took nearly all of human history to reach that first billion. The next seven arrived in about two centuries. So what changed, and where did everybody end up?

cards.headline: Soap, food and medicine
cards.body: For almost all of history, our numbers crept up slowly. Around 1800 they reached about 1 billion. Then the curve bent sharply upward, and on 15 November 2022 the UN marked the world passing 8 billion. The main reason is that people live longer: better public health, nutrition, hygiene and medicine. Humanity's great boom was powered less by magic than by soap, good food and a doctor down the road.

cards.context: Going from 7 to 8 billion took 12 years. The next billion should take about 15, arriving around 2037. The UN expects the total to peak at about 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s. Think of a car that has taken its foot off the gas: still rolling forward, but coasting toward a stop.

cards.headline: Where everyone lives
cards.body: People are not spread like butter on toast. The Asia-Pacific region alone is home to about 60% of humanity. It holds the two giants, too: in April 2023, by UN estimates, India overtook China as the most populous country, after China's population had peaked in 2022 and begun to fall.

cards.headline: A lopsided planet
cards.body: Remember Level 4's Equator, splitting Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres? The split is not fair. About 87% of people live in the Northern Hemisphere, which also holds about two-thirds of the land. If you're reading this, the odds say you're north of the Equator too.

mascot.line: Nearly nine in ten of us on the top half of the globe. The Southern Hemisphere has plenty of elbow room.

cards.headline: Eight billion: counted
learned: About 1 billion people around 1800, 8 billion in 2022
Growth is slowing; a peak near 10.3 billion is expected
About 60% live in Asia-Pacific, about 87% north of the Equator

questions.prompt: About how many people lived on Earth around 1800?

options.label: About 100 million
options.rationale: Too few: the total was already about ten times that.

options.label: About 4 billion
options.rationale: That came much later, in the 20th century.

questions.explanation: Around 1800 the world population was about 1 billion. It passed 8 billion in 2022.

questions.prompt: What mainly drove the huge rise in world population after 1800?

options.label: Families everywhere suddenly had twice as many children
options.rationale: The big change was survival, not birth rates alone.

options.label: People moved into cities
options.rationale: Cities grew, but that is not what multiplied the total.

options.label: Migration opened up empty continents
options.rationale: Moving people around does not add to the total.

options.label: People lived longer, thanks to better health, food and medicine

questions.explanation: Longer lives, from improvements in public health, nutrition, hygiene and medicine, drove the growth.

questions.prompt: Using Level 4's Equator: which half of the globe is home to about 87% of people?

options.label: The Southern Hemisphere
options.rationale: Only a small share of people live south of the Equator.

options.label: The half inside the tropics
options.rationale: The tropics are a belt, not a hemisphere.

options.label: The Western Hemisphere
options.rationale: The Equator splits north from south, not east from west.

questions.explanation: About 87% of people live in the Northern Hemisphere, north of the Equator, where about two-thirds of the land is.
